questions.question: What is an Operating System?
options: Software that manages computer hardware and lets you run apps
questions.explanation: An OS is the main software that manages your computer's hardware, memory, files, and runs other programs.

questions.question: Which shortcut opens File Explorer in Windows?
questions.explanation: Win + E opens File Explorer. This is one of the most useful Windows shortcuts.

questions.question: What does Task Manager help you do?
options: See running programs and close stuck apps
questions.explanation: Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) shows running programs, CPU/RAM usage, and lets you end stuck apps.

questions.question: Which Linux command lists files in the current folder?
questions.explanation: ls (list) shows all files and folders in the current directory in Linux.

questions.question: What does the 'cd' command do in Linux?
questions.explanation: cd = Change Directory. Example: 'cd Documents' moves you into the Documents folder.

questions.question: Which shortcut copies selected text or files?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + C = Copy. Then use Ctrl + V to paste. Ctrl + X = Cut (move instead of copy).

questions.question: Which OS is free and open source?
questions.explanation: Linux is free and open source — anyone can see, modify, and share the code. Ubuntu is the most popular version.

questions.question: What does Ctrl + Z do?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + Z = Undo. It reverses your last action. Works in almost every app.

questions.question: What does 'mkdir' command do in Linux?
questions.explanation: mkdir = Make Directory. Example: 'mkdir myproject' creates a new folder called myproject.

questions.question: To make your computer start faster, what should you do in Task Manager?
questions.explanation: Go to Startup tab in Task Manager and disable apps you don't need at startup. This speeds up boot time.

questions.question: Which shortcut locks your Windows computer?
questions.explanation: Win + L instantly locks your computer. Always lock when leaving your desk!

questions.question: What is the Linux command to delete a file?
questions.explanation: rm = Remove. Example: 'rm oldfile.txt' deletes the file. Be careful — Linux doesn't have a Recycle Bin by default!
